scope: Flight controls. Every help screen includes this same clearly labelled Flight controls block. Menu and mission-dialog confirmation remains a separate context; Return in a menu confirms its focused choice and never fires a weapon.

bindings.detail: Cycle equipped Main Laser, Mining Laser, Salvage Cutter and EMP Blaster. Update the persistent weapon indicator immediately; retain the current hold.

Hold Return to operate the selected weapon: fire the Main Laser, mine with the Mining Laser, cut with the Salvage Cutter, or charge/fire EMP. Release to stop the held action. Require a fresh press after a weapon change, readiness transition or interruption. Releasing Return retains the hold.
Activate fitted ECM directly, subject to actual energy and cooldown requirements. ECM stays separate from weapon selection.
End automatic hold/guidance and stop the active tool. Return control to the player while preserving momentum.

footer: W: CHANGE WEAPON | RETURN: FIRE | E: ECM | Q: RELEASE HOLD
automaticSelection: Targeting any disabled ship for salvage selects fitted Salvage Cutter immediately. Targeting an asteroid selects fitted Mining Laser immediately. Selection never fires. W overrides the default for the current target without releasing hold.
helpPolicy: Generate README controls, help-screen flight blocks, contextual footers and the salvage guide labels from these four bindings. No help topic may assign another key to these actions.
Keep the primary Return action label Fire for every weapon. Mining, cutting and EMP charging are explained beneath it and in the actual weapon/activity indicator, not by changing the binding label.
All flight views and help topics use Change weapon rather than alternating between Change tool and Change weapon; Q is Release hold rather than Off, Back or Cancel.
Equipment prerequisites and temporarily blocked states are explained alongside the binding without remapping its key. Menu navigation and confirmation are clearly distinguished from Flight controls.

The game implementation must consume the shared control authority for every help topic and visible action hint, with regression coverage that enumerates all actual help screens. Generated authority requires native integration and runtime verification.

helpTopics.title: Flight
helpTopics.detail: Read the persistent WEAPON indicator before firing. W and Return never release an established hold.

helpTopics.title: Combat
helpTopics.detail: W selects the equipped Main Laser; hold Return to fire it. E activates ECM separately.

helpTopics.title: Targeting and automatic hold
helpTopics.detail: Targeting establishes supported guidance. Q releases the hold; changing or firing the selected weapon retains it.

helpTopics.title: Asteroid mining
helpTopics.detail: Asteroid targeting establishes a safe target-relative hold and selects the fitted Mining Laser. W can select Main Laser instead; held Return then breaks the rock into much smaller chunks, leaving strictly less than 5% of its original mass recoverable. Most rock disintegrates permanently. Collect surviving chunks with fitted scoops; changing weapon or firing does not release the hold before the parent breaks apart.

helpTopics.title: Disabled ships and salvage
helpTopics.detail: Acquiring a disabled salvage ship selects the fitted Salvage Cutter. Hold Return to cut eligible material; W can select another fitted weapon while retaining hold.

helpTopics.title: EMP
helpTopics.detail: W selects fitted EMP Blaster; hold Return to charge/fire it. The weapon indicator reports actual charge and readiness.

helpTopics.title: ECM
helpTopics.detail: E activates fitted ECM. ECM has its own actual energy/cooldown checks and does not replace the selected weapon.

helpTopics.title: Navigation
helpTopics.detail: These are flight bindings. Q releases automatic hold/guidance while in flight; station and chart navigation keep their own clearly labelled Back action.

helpTopics.title: Equipment and fitting
helpTopics.detail: Fitted weapons participate in the W cycle. Menu Return confirms the selected fitting action; flight Return fires the selected weapon.

helpTopics.title: Shipyard and ship gallery
helpTopics.detail: These are flight bindings after launch. Ship selection and purchase use their explicit menu confirmation controls.

helpTopics.title: Inventory and recovered equipment
helpTopics.detail: Held cargo is not fitted equipment. Fit a recovered compatible weapon before it is available in the W cycle.

helpTopics.title: Market and cargo
helpTopics.detail: These are flight bindings. Cargo trading retains its explicit menu actions and never fires a weapon.

helpTopics.title: Mission contacts and dialogs
helpTopics.detail: Mission dialogs use their labelled Confirm/Back actions. In flight, all mission weapons and salvage use these same shared bindings.

helpTopics.title: Commander status
helpTopics.detail: Status describes fitted equipment; the persistent flight WEAPON indicator shows what Return will operate.

helpTopics.title: Settings and general help
helpTopics.detail: Every help topic includes the same Flight controls block. Context-specific menu instructions remain visibly separate.

asteroidDestruction: Asteroid targeting establishes a safe target-relative hold and selects the fitted Mining Laser. W can select Main Laser instead; held Return then breaks the rock into much smaller chunks, leaving strictly less than 5% of its original mass recoverable. Most rock disintegrates permanently. Collect surviving chunks with fitted scoops; changing weapon or firing does not release the hold before the parent breaks apart.
selectionRules: Immediately on acquiring any disabled ship for salvage, automatically select the fitted Salvage Cutter. Immediately on acquiring an asteroid, automatically select the fitted Mining Laser. Do not wait for stable hold. This is selection only: extraction remains inhibited until safe range, aim, motion and permissions are satisfied, followed by a fresh Return press.

Apply the default once for each new target acquisition, regardless of the tool used on the previous target. W can override it for the current target. Completing approach or refreshing the HUD must not overwrite that current-target choice or repeatedly reselect the default.

After the automatic selection, W allows the player to choose Main Laser instead, then a fresh held Return fires it while maintaining the same hold. W can select the appropriate extraction tool again without another approach or target selection.

If the extraction tool is absent, state Salvage Cutter not fitted or Mining Laser not fitted and retain a safe hold. Never replace an attempted extraction shot with combat fire. The player may explicitly select an equipped Main Laser and press Return to destroy the target.

A wreck can be cut only at an eligible recoverable section. Occupied, claimed or mission-protected targets display their state; merely holding position does not make them abandoned or grant salvage rights. A living ship must meet the existing abandonment/disablement and custody rules before extraction is enabled.
Active stations retain their docking action and protection; this capital-ship hold rule does not convert an operational station into a destructible salvage target.

Main Laser damage follows normal combat and legal rules. Destroying an asteroid produces much smaller collectible chunks with total recoverable mass strictly below 5% of the original rock; the rest disintegrates permanently. This is poor-yield salvage, not normal Mining Laser extraction. Destruction of ship systems can lose recoverable components. Depletion, destruction and disappearance are separate outcomes.
holdRules: Selecting a capital-sized ship or asteroid automatically approaches a safe surface-relative work position and matches drift and spin when the matching guidance module is installed. Acquisition never fires a tool. Show APPROACHING, MATCHING MOTION, HOLDING or an explicit BLOCKED reason.

The hull's actual surface and swept protrusions determine clearance. Work within the selected tool's real range, acceleration and manoeuvring limits. Refuse an impossible hold safely, without teleporting, collision-producing pursuit or unlimited thrust.

Hold continues between extraction bursts, after switching to the Main Laser, while the Main Laser fires, after a section is depleted and while released material is collected. A combat tool choice is not a request to leave orbit.
The large target remains the primary lock. Collecting a fragment or changing an accessible work section never substitutes a child object for the parent ship or asteroid.

Missing Mining/Salvage Module prevents that specialized automatic hold and reports the precise requirement. Ordinary manual flight, main-laser targeting and manual use of actually fitted work tools remain available. Core tier alone does not grant either specialist module.

Held Return operates only the explicitly selected tool. The Main Laser uses the current supported combat mount; Mining Laser uses its supported mining facing and a corresponding safe work pose; Salvage Cutter uses its separate utility fitting. Changing tool does not replace or remove any combat laser.
Mining or cutting automatically enables fitted Fuel Scoops for reachable released material. No extra scoop activation, fragment retargeting or Auto salvage confirmation is needed.

Collect through the real scoop aperture with safe relative movement and sufficient unreserved hold space. No cargo teleport or unbounded tractor effect. An inaccessible or oversized lot stays in space and produces a clear reason.

Releasing Return stops the beam but retains target-relative hold. Already reachable material can finish collection. Finite section progress, remaining ore and issued item identities survive retargeting and current-format save/load without rerolling or duplication.

A destroyed parent ends its hold and reports destruction. A fully extracted parent that still exists reports Salvage complete or Mining complete and stays selected in a safe hold until cancelled. A successfully scooped single item reports Collected rather than Target lost.

Q, deliberate manual steering/throttle or selecting another primary target ends guidance immediately and stops the tool, preserving momentum. W and Return are tool inputs, not manual flight overrides.
Changing the target filter cancels the current automatic hold and firing before the new selection cycle. Opening target details does not cancel or secretly retarget it.

Incoming attack interrupts extraction and warns. Any safety cancellation is visible and does not silently re-engage; require a fresh player command and a fresh Return press before tool use resumes. Space combat, heat and collisions remain live during hold.
XYZZY explicitly fits both specialist modules, Mining Laser, Salvage Cutter and Fuel Scoops. Resource cheats remain independent; tool selection still never fires automatically.

weaponIndicator.label: WEAPON
weaponIndicator.placement: Persistent instrument row immediately above the central scanner, using reserved layout space. Keep it visible in every flight view and drawing mode, with or without a target or expanded target panel, at compact and full-screen sizes.
weaponIndicator.content: Show the currently selected Main Laser, Mining Laser, Salvage Cutter or EMP Blaster, followed by its actual state. For Main Laser also show the fitted laser variant and current mount/view where space permits. Use NONE only when no compatible weapon/tool is fitted; a temporarily blocked fitting retains its name and the reason.
weaponIndicator.stateAuthority: Read selected fitting, readiness, charging progress, cooldown and obstruction from authoritative runtime state. Do not infer the selected weapon from target type, the last beam drawn or a transient notification. Show one applicable current state; selection alone never implies readiness or firing.
weaponIndicator.updates: Refresh immediately on W changes, automatic cutter/mining selection, fitting changes and view/mount changes. The same selected-weapon authority determines what Return operates and what the HUD names. Update the label before accepting another tool-use input.
weaponIndicator.presentation: Keep the weapon name visible continuously, not only in a toast, target detail panel or help screen. Status uses words as well as optional colour. Preserve the compact fixed font and a reserved row so it cannot overlap scanner, shields, missile rack or contextual help.
examples: WEAPON: SALVAGE CUTTER | WAITING FOR HOLD
weaponIndicator.exampleNotice: Examples illustrate display copy only. Numeric charge progress must come from the actual charge state.
weaponIndicator.help: W: CHANGE WEAPON | RETURN: FIRE | E: ECM | Q: RELEASE HOLD. Keep this same control wording for every weapon; explain mining, cutting or EMP charging through the weapon name, actual activity state and secondary help text.
